title: UGT recipe (draft 1)
description: What was run, for which task, on what, and how it was proved. Provisional: recipe_format names the draft, and each breaking change before v1 bumps it.

commit.description: Full commit SHA the package was built from.

release.description: Release artifact used instead of a source build, when applicable.

task.description: The user's task as an output, in plain words.

build.description: Builds $UGT_IMAGE (Compose: $UGT_IMAGE-<service>) from the recipe folder or a pinned Git context, never a local clone: the build fetches the pinned source itself. Skipped when a verified image is pulled under the same name.

run.description: Does the task on the files in inputs/ and writes outputs/.

check.description: Fails unless the task happened, for any input: every declared output exists and has the right structure and plausible values. Never tied to one input's content; that belongs in sample.check.

sample.description: A known input whose correct output is predictable, so the recipe can be verified on a clean machine before it touches the user's input. Required except for agent installs.

setup.description: Puts the known input at the paths in inputs, from the recipe folder or a pinned public download, or by generating it.

check.description: Run after run and check on the sample's output; fails unless the output contains what the known input predicts.

licence.description: SPDX identifier of the upstream project, plus a note if it affects sharing or hosting.

command.description: Exact POSIX shell command, run from the workspace root. The executor sets UGT_IMAGE (the image name), UGT_NAME (the prefix for container, volume and Compose project names; also exported as COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME) and UGT_ARCH (amd64 or arm64, for --platform linux/$UGT_ARCH unless the recipe works on one architecture only), and selects the engine through DOCKER_CONTEXT and BUILDX_BUILDER. Commands use those names and never choose the engine themselves.

allOf.description: No engine, context or builder selection.

path.description: Workspace-relative path with forward slashes; never absolute, home-relative or escaping the workspace.
